texts.facts: 1. In this case, a claim petition filed by the petitioner u/s 166 Mv Act 2. Brief facts of the case are that on 28.02.2018 at about 3.00 pm, petitioner/injured alongwith his friend Ashutosh Kumar were travelling on Scooty bearing no. DL-2SR-0376. On reaching Village Mamura, Gali no. 6, Sec.-66, NOIDA, a tractor bearing no. UP-13AV5659, suddenly came and hit the scooty, resulting which petitioner suffered injuries. The driver of erring tractor failed to take due care and was negligent in driving while egressing a Gali in speed without making proper watch, horn and indicator and accident occurred due to his rash and negligent driving of driver of offending Pankaj Kumar Ray vs Jaswant on 26 September, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31172659/ 1 vehicle. Petitioner/injured suffered fracture on his left hand and leg/knee. 3. He was firstly taken to Om Hospital, NOIDA and then to Fortis Hospital, NOIDA and remained admitted there from 28.02.2018 to 02.03.2018. That till date, petitioner had not resumed its original physical stature. 4. Further, Medical Board of Pt. Madan Mohan Hospital, Malviya Nagar, New Delhi sent disability report dated 02.11.2021 noticing 14% permanent physical impairment in relation to his left upper limb and left lower limb. 5. An FIR bearing No. 0356/2018 u/s 279/338 IPC PS Phase III, District-Gautambudh Nagar, U.P. was registered in this case. 6. In response to petition, respondent No.1 and 2 and Respondent MACT No. 736/18 Pankaj Kumar Ray v. Jaswant Page No. 2 of 20 BK no.3 appeared and filed their respective replies. 7. From the pleadings of parties, the following issues were framed on 17.11.2018 by Predecessor of this Tribunal: 1. Whether the injured Pankaj Kumar Ray suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 28.02.2018 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. UP-13AV-5659 (Tractor) being driven by R1, owned by R2 and insured with R3? OPP. 2. Whether the injured is entitled to any compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?OPP 3. Relief. 8. Petitioner Pankaj Kumar Ray tendered his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. He relied upon various documents including the discharge summary and medical bills Ex. PW-1/1 (OSR) to PW-1/10. He was cross-examined by learned counsel for insurance company. 9. No other evidence has been led on behalf of petitioner. 10. None of the respondent led any evidence. It is well settled that the proceedings before the Claims Tribunal are in the nature of inquiry and the finding of rash and negligent driving by driver of the offending vehicle is to be returned only at the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities. The factors noted above are sufficient to conclude that preponderance of probability is made out showing negligence of MACT No. 736/18 Pankaj Kumar Ray v. Jaswant Page No. 3 of 20 BK respondent No. 1 in causing the accident. 14. In the present case, police after investigation had filed charge-sheet against respondent no.1 under section 279/338 of IPC which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent in causing the accident. The IO has filed Detailed Accident Report before this Tribunal. 15. Further, in his examination in chief PW-1/ Victim/ Injured / Petitioner deposed on the lines of petition and facts as already noted above. Further, on perusal of his cross-examination, he told that he alongwith his friend Ashutosh Kumar was going on scooty driven by himself. He told that truck was driven at high speed without giving any horn and indication resulting the present accident. The speed of said offending truck was 40 to 60 KMH. He further denied the suggestion that accident took place due to his negligence. He and his friend were wearing the helmet. He further denied the suggestion that no such accident took place. 16. In the present case, police after investigation had filed charge-sheet against respondent no.1 under section 279/338 of IPC which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent in causing the accident. 17. Further, there is a chargesheet against the respondent no.1 filed for the offence u/s 279, 337, 338 IPC. Further, respondent no.1 did not choose to MACT No. 736/18 Pankaj Kumar Ray v. Jaswant Page No. 4 of 20 BK lead any evidence to contrary.
texts.arguments: In National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. In National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet u/s 279/338 IPC are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. At this stage, before proceeding further, by rely upon the judgments of C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair, R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. and Baker v. Willoughby which are referred and relied in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343 decided by Hon'ble SC, it can be noted that the provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Pankaj Kumar Ray vs Jaswant on 26 September, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31172659/ 3 Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. 19. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is MACT No. 736/18 Pankaj Kumar Ray v. Jaswant Page No. 5 of 20 BK awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iii) Future medical expenses. Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). (vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity). 19.1. It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii)(b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life. 19.3. Assessment of pecuniary damages under Item (i) and under Item (ii) (a) do not pose much Pankaj Kumar Ray vs Jaswant on 26 September, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31172659/ 4 difficulty as they involve reimbursement of actuals and are easily ascertainable from the evidence. 19.5. Assessment of non-pecuniary damages--Items (iv), (v) and (vi)-- involves determination of l u m p s u m a m o u n t s w i t h r e f e r e n c e t o c i r c u m s t a n c e s s u c h a s a g e , n a t u r e o f injury/deprivation/disability suffered by the claimant and the effect thereof on the future life of the claimant. 19.6. It was observed by Hon'ble Sc in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability--Item (ii) (a). 19.7. This means that the Tribunal should consider and decide with reference to the MACT No. 736/18 Pankaj Kumar Ray v. Jaswant Page No. 7 of 20 BK evidence: (i) whether the disablement is permanent or temporary; (ii) if the disablement is permanent, whether it is permanent total disablement or permanent partial disablement; (iii) if the disablement percentage is expressed with reference to any specific limb, then the effect of such disablement of the limb on the functioning of the entire body,that is, the permanent disability suffered by the person. If the Tribunal concludes that there is no permanent disability then there is no question of proceeding further and determining the loss of future earning capacity. Further in such case of Raj Kumar MACT No. 736/18 Pankaj Kumar Ray v. Jaswant Page No. 11 of 20 BK Vs. , the Hon'ble Supreme Court laid down a three step approach to decide compensation for the injured persons who have suffered permanent disability and same are as under: i) Tribunal should see as to what the injured can do inspite of permanent disability and what the injured cannot do: At this stage, it is relevant to the refer to the judgment of A. V. Padma & Ors. Vs., R. Venugopal & Ors. (2012) 3 Supreme Court Cases 378: MACT No. 736/18 Pankaj Kumar Ray v. Jaswant Page No. 14 of 20 BK "...... In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". In the case of illiterate claimants, the Tribunal is allowed to consider the request for lumpsum payment for effecting purchase of any movable property such as agricultural implements, rickshaws etc. to earn a living. Moreover, in the case of literate persons, the Tribunal may resort to the procedure indicated in guideline No. (i) only if, having regard to the age, fiscal background and strata of the society to which the claimant belongs and such other considerations, the Tribunal thinks that in the larger interest of the claimant and with a view to ensure the safety of the compensation awarded, it is necessary to invest the amount of compensation in long term fixed MACT No. 736/18 Pankaj Kumar Ray v. Jaswant Page No. 15 of 20 BK deposit. It needs to be clarified that the above guidelines were issued by this Court only to safeguard the interests of the Pankaj Kumar Ray vs Jaswant on 26 September, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31172659/ 10 claimants, particularly the minors, illiterates and others whose amounts are sought to be withdrawn on some fictitious grounds. 11 (a) The Bank shall not permit any joint name(s) to be added in the savings bank account or fixed deposit accounts of the claimant(s) i.e. the savings bank account(s) of the claimant(s) shall be an individual savings bank account(s) and MACT No. 736/18 Pankaj Kumar Ray v. Jaswant Page No. 17 of 20 BK not a joint account(s).
